text:
maya: heads up — support ticket T-4351: customer reported sudden p99 spike (~2.4x) on continuous-batcher for their small-prompt traffic around 09:12 UTC. They say it started after a traffic pattern change.

support-bot: linked ticket: https://redwood.support/tickets/T-4351, customer tenant id: tenant-acme-17. attached traces: trace_id=trc_0a1b2c3d

sam: I pulled the dashboards — aggregate p50/95 look fine but p99 and tail count jump on the continuous-batcher service. See query I ran: `sum(rate(batcher_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)` shows heavier mass at >1s buckets for tenant-acme-17.

jordan: curious if this is the usual tiny-prompt problem (lots of 20-50 token requests). Could be coalesce waiting for peers and then holding tiny prompts longer due to inter-arrival jitter.

lee: can we repro? asking customer for a minimal script. also checking if auth/billing changed — CPU/GPU usage looked normal.

maya: customer sent repro: simple loop sending 30 requests/sec of 30-token prompts with 8 concurrent clients. They see p99 at ~1.8s vs baseline ~0.6s. Provided logs and a short client.

sam: repro locally with k6 and their payload reproduced p99 spike when we enabled continuous batching with default hold-window=8ms and max-batch-size=64. When we lowered hold-window for that tenant to 2ms p99 improved dramatically.

jordan: interesting — sounds like "hold-window entropy" where jitter in inter-arrival times causes batches to form with many tiny prompts that then sit waiting for fullness? I noticed our batcher has a dynamic backoff that increases hold for high CPU leftovers; might be interacting badly.

lee: posted quick diff to canary: set tenant override for tenant-acme-17: `{ "continuous_batch": { "hold_window_ms": 2, "max_batch_size": 32, "min_flush_ms": 1 } }`. Deployed to canary pool.

infra-bot: deploy canary successful on pool gc-canary-4. version: infer-batcher@v3.8.1-rc.

sam: after canary, customer p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 0.62s on their repro. However, overall cluster throughput for that pool dipped ~6% under mixed workloads. tradeoff expected.

maya: customer confirmed improvement in production for a subset of routes after tenant override. They want a permanent fix that doesn't regress throughput.

jordan: follow-up investigation: we saw correlation with inter-request jitter distribution shifting from uniform to bursty with microbursts. The continuous coalescer logic uses a leaky-window counter which ramps hold_window_ms up when it sees per-core work backlog. That ramping plus microbursts caused some requests to be delayed unpredictably.

lee: options: 1) keep per-tenant hold-window overrides (safe, conservative). 2) add special-casing for small payloads: auto-route small prompts to a fast-path with reduced coalesce. 3) cap adaptive ramping so it never exceeds X ms for small prompt tenants.

maya: customer prefers option 2 if low-risk. they care most about tail latency for small prompts.

sam: quick mitigation we rolled: tenant override + enable small-payload fast-path flag on canary. config snippet we used: 
```json
{
  "tenant_overrides": {
    "tenant-acme-17": {
      "continuous_batch": {
        "hold_window_ms": 2,
        "max_batch_size": 32,
        "payload_fast_path_threshold_tokens": 64,
        "enable_fast_path": true
      }
    }
  }
}
```

jordan: added instrumented metrics for fast-path routing: `batcher.fastpath.routed_total`, `batcher.fastpath.latency_p99` and a tag by tenant. will land on main after internal review.

lee: also filed follow-up ticket INF-9923 to add cap to adaptive ramping and a unit test for jittery arrivals.

maya: notes for postmortem: timeline, customer repro, canary changes, mitigations, perf tradeoffs, plan for safe rollout. assigning action owners: sam -> perf validation across mixed workloads, jordan -> metrics + tests, lee -> rollout plan & DCO.

support-bot: updated ticket T-4351 with fix notes and asked customer for 24h confirmation window.

maya: thanks team. if anyone sees other tenants with similar microburst signatures, ping this thread. :thumbsup:

sam: one more reproducible command we used (k6 snippet):
```bash
k6 run --vus 8 --duration 1m -e PAYLOAD='{"input":"short prompt here"}' ./scripts/hammer-batcher.js
```

jordan: saved traces and flamegraphs to s3://redwood-ops/batcher-traces/T-4351/ for postmortem.

lee: leaving this on watch for next 24h, will revert tenant override if we see throughput regression on main pool.

maya: closing loop once customer ACKs.
